findings.title: Retain forwarded focus reports in native settlement accounting
findings.body: Must-fix — HIGH correctness/authority: validated original-attachment view changes in src/daemon.rs:950-1003 forward CSI I/O through `protocol_input_authorized`, whose enqueue sets `native: false`; consequently `Input::write_to` checks authority but does not call `forward_native` or retain an unknown native batch. Start an application through accounted shell execution that enables focus reporting, pause it before input consumption, acquire native control without other raw input, and send an outer focus transition: the daemon can write the focus event while `ownership.unsettled` remains empty, then yield/offer/accept can issue `mode: safe`, after which the resumed application consumes old-generation focus input. Route focus through `input_authorized` or enable native accounting in this helper without recording human activity, retaining original-connection and dispatch-time checks, and add a paused-consumer focus/yield regression that rejects a safe offer. This false-safe-grant path is outside the exception allowing genuinely unknown Codex work to block transfer indefinitely.

E03SecurityReview.coverage_summary:
Verdict: PASS for the explicitly amended CURRENT delivery security scope. No unaddressed security findings survived source-to-sink tracing; no unwaived HIGH blocks current landing. This is the fresh e03 current-delivery security round 1 only, not a reset of historical review caps or a complete-broker acceptance PASS.

Checklist: 24 applicable static-review checks; must-fix 0, should-fix 0; score = 100 × (24−0−0)/24 = 100%. Checks covered: capability minting/kind binding; PTY lifetime/generation; exclusive authority/revocation; private recovery; raw CLI input; execute/epoch/wake continuations; automatic/managed startup; native keys/repeats/literal prefix; paste/mouse and intercepted gesture tails; focus/protocol replies; cooperative reservation/offer/accept; explicit force; ordinary cancellation; conditional keep/withdraw; original-connection view/activity; atomic consent/eligibility; unknown native settlement; same-instance discovery; exact typed request identities; closed structured operations/outcomes; privacy; owned cleanup; bounded queues/accounting; patched dependencies and preserved regression consumers. This score is review-checklist scoring, not measured code coverage.

Key evidence: src/control.rs:824–840 binds each opaque reference to its daemon-minted kind; :1078–1087 checks current reference/controller/generation and target lifetime. src/runtime.rs:52–68 revalidates queued input and records native forwarding before I/O; daemon input/execute admission is at src/daemon.rs:1058–1158. Shell continuations recover their originating authority at daemon.rs:287–350, while integrations/zsh/adapter.zsh:134–147 clears BUFFER when final acceptance fails. Native input routes converge on src/tui/control.rs:601–623, with FIFO original-connection work and no transport-error replay at :137–229; mouse tails are consumed at :967–1003. Automatic terminal replies are internally classified, not a public protocol-label bypass.

Safe-grant controls remain fail-closed: src/control.rs:1181–1208 refuses to clear native-input unknown, :700–722 requires an empty retained-call ledger for offer acceptance, and :1573–1607 revalidates conditional authority, consent revisions, eligibility, warning completion and settlement. Revocation retains old calls, force exposes unresolved-call warnings, and ordinary cancellation grants nobody. Original attachment provenance is checked independently of borrowed input capabilities. Corresponding real-daemon/native tests inspect actual target effects and retained calls rather than only successful receipts.

Structured operations require the exact bound terminal/instance/session and applicable turn/item/typed request ID (src/codex.rs:757–881), then revalidate at queue consumption before Authority::forward (:1218–1253). Unknown/reused response attribution stays unknown (:1694–1733); request closure and whole-turn completion do not drain unrelated native work. Permission encoding is request-only accept/decline, never a session grant. Auxiliary title threads do not replace the established root. Local provider transport is a generated private Unix socket, not a caller-selected remote WebSocket endpoint (:321–385, :1834–1897).

Privacy/cleanup inspection covered private 0700 roots, 0600 no-follow credential copies, redacted public facts/evidence, unbound-launch RAII cleanup, terminal/backend failure paths and birth-qualified process cleanup. Cargo.lock:1309–1327 resolves time 0.3.47/time-core 0.1.8; no second time entry was found. Cargo.toml:5 honestly declares Rust 1.88; the independent showcase remains 1.86.

Fowler-smell assessment: Long Method is visible in daemon::dispatch (src/daemon.rs:936–1432) and codex::handle_message (src/codex.rs:1294–1753); string/JSON-driven state also warrants care. These are maintainability observations, not demonstrated security defects or current must/should-fix findings. Existing authority and provider boundaries avoid duplicating authorization policy in each input consumer.

Verification provenance: I performed read-only source, test and evidence inspection; I ran no builds, tests, linters, formatters, daemons, payloads, network requests or model calls, and made no repository edits or contact with other reviewers. Reported runtime results are parent-observed evidence, not verification run by me. The recorded full Codex acceptance remains FAILED with zero meaningful turns at its first safe offer, and e03s08 remains failing.
